item.title: ASP.NET Web API: Serving Binary Files and Fixing Content Type Issues
item.description:
“ASP.NET Web API: Serving Binary Files and Fixing Content Type Issues”

Developing APIs that serve downloadable content, such as executables or compressed archives, requires careful handling of file streams and proper configuration of HTTP response headers, particularly the Content-Type. How do expert developers reliably return file content as application/octet-stream across different versions of the .NET framework, from classic Web API to modern .NET Core?

Delivering Files via HttpResponseMessage and StreamContent (Classic Web API)

When working with older or traditional ASP.NET Web API projects, one reliable pattern involves using HttpResponseMessage directly, wrapping the file stream in a StreamContent.

item.title: ASP.NET Web API: Binding Comma-Separated Values to Arrays and Lists
item.description:
“ASP.NET Web API: Binding Comma-Separated Values to Arrays and Lists”

Diverse Approaches for Array Parameter Binding in Web APIs

Developers have devised several distinct techniques to handle the automatic conversion of delimited string inputs into strongly-typed arrays or lists. The best approach often depends on the specific ASP.NET version and whether external tooling like Swagger integration is critical.

1. Utilizing the [FromUri] Attribute for Simple Arrays (Query String Style)

For basic array binding directly from the query string in older Web API versions, explicitly marking the parameter with [FromUri] can sometimes work if the client sends repeated keys.
